title: Tenant isolation and SSO/Crypto proofing: acceptance checklist and evidence runbook
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: This PRD describes the acceptance criteria and evidence collection runbook for tenant isolation guarantees across Private/VPC deployments with a focus on SAML/SSO assertions, customer-specific KMS keys, HSM-backed attestation, and operator RBAC separation. Background: Several enterprise customers require deterministic proof that (1) tenant data cannot be accessed by other tenants or operators without explicit narrow escalation, (2) customer-managed keys can be rotated and audited, and (3) SSO assertions and audit logs are retained, timestamped, and tamper-evident. Goals: 1) Define verifiable acceptance tests that product, security, and customer ops can run during onboarding. 2) Produce a signed checklist and artifact bundle per customer that satisfies SOC2/ISO-style auditors. 3) Ensure runtime controls (RBAC, SAML assertion encryption, key separation, audit immutability) are implemented and observable. Non-goals: We are not redesigning the underlying serving runtime in this ticket; performance tuning for high-throughput key operations will be tracked separately. Assumptions: Private deployments will have a managed control plane and a customer-owned KMS/HSM or a dedicated managed key. The infra team will provide temporary test tenants and operator accounts for verification. Proposed solution: Provide a structured checklist, automated test harnesses (SAML assertion replay, KMS rotation simulation, operator access attempt logs), and a reproducible evidence export (signed audit bundle with logs, key rotation records, SAML metadata and assertion samples, RBAC policy snapshots). The runbook will map each acceptance criterion to specific test steps and expected artifacts. Success criteria: acceptance checklist passed by security and customer, evidence bundle validated by at least one third-party auditor or an internal compliance reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: SAML: Service provider metadata is published and verified; SAML assertions are signed and encrypted end-to-end between IdP and tenant runtime with a confirmed encryption algorithm (AES256-GCM or equivalent).
SSO: Single sign-on sessions cannot be accepted by another tenant; SAML assertion audience restriction and InResponseTo checks are validated in tests.

RBAC: Operator roles are scoped to specific customer tenants; separation of duties demonstrated by a red-team test where an operator lacking ‘cust-admin’ role cannot retrieve tenant keys or decrypt payloads.
KMS: Customer-key-per-tenant model implemented; key usage logs show decrypt/encrypt operations with tenant-id tags and key-version metadata.
HSM: For HSM-backed KMS, attestation artifacts (quote, certificate chain) included and verified against the vendor’s root.

Audit logs: Append-only audit stream with tamper-evidence (hash chaining or signature) for auth, key ops, and operator actions; logs retain required retention period and are exportable to customer SIEM.
Proof bundle: Evidence package contains sample SAML assertions, RBAC policy snapshot (timestamped), key rotation event with before/after key IDs, and signed audit log segment for a chosen 24h window.
Operational: Automated checks and manual test steps are documented and executed in staging; results and failure modes recorded in the runbook.
Regression: Changes to SSO/KMS/RBAC code paths include regression tests that exercise these acceptance points in CI.
signoff_checklist: Product: Verify acceptance criteria mapped to product requirements and confirm compatibility with existing onboarding flow.
Security: Threat model reviewed and signed; all high/critical issues mitigated or accepted with documented risk statement.
Infra/Eng: Integration tests green (ENG-8421) and deployment templates updated; load test results for KMS/HSM path recorded.
Compliance: Evidence bundle reviewed vs. SOC2/ISO control mapping; retention and access policy approved.
Solutions/SE: Onboarding guide updated; one pilot customer walkthrough completed successfully.
Legal: Contract addendum for customer-managed keys or zero-knowledge custody reviewed where required.
Customer Ops: Customer-specific test run completed with signed acceptance form from the customer SRE/security lead.
Release: Release notes and limited rollout schedule approved by PM, Security, and SRE owners.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout in Private environments: phase 1 (5 customers, manual verification), phase 2 (20 customers, automated verification), phase 3 (full enabled). Each phase runs for 7 days. Telemetry: KMS latency, assertion failure rates, operator access denials, audit export success rate. Roll-forward only if all critical metrics are within thresholds and two independent security reviewers sign off.
rollback_criteria: Any increase >1% in SAML assertion failures tied to encryption/audience errors compared to baseline.
Any operator privilege bypass reproduction during red-team or CI tests.
KMS decrypt error rate >0.5% or key rotation causing failed decrypts for active sessions.
Audit export failures or evidence bundle generation errors in >2 of 5 canary customers.
risks: Interoperability gaps between customer IdPs causing assertion encryption failures.
KMS performance impact at scale if each tenant uses separate keys causing cold-start HSM latencies.
Operator error during emergency key rotation leading to brief availability impact.
Incomplete or inconsistent audit log tagging makes evidence bundles hard to reconcile for auditors.
mitigations: Pre-onboarding checklist for IdP capabilities and recommended SAML profiles (signed+encrypted).
Benchmarking matrix for KMS/HSM cold-start and warm paths; recommend caching/connection pooling patterns for customer-specific keys.
Operator runbooks, dry-run rotations in staging, and mandatory two-person approval for production rotations.
Standardized log schema with tenant_id, request_id, key_id, and sha256 chaining; automated validation of the bundle before signoff.
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Decided to require encrypted SAML assertions for all Private deployments (Priya Nair, Security). 2025-02-18: Chosen artifact format for evidence bundles: gzipped JSONL logs + signed manifest (sha256) with timestamped RBAC snapshot (Liam O'Connor, Eng Lead). 2025-02-25: Opted for per-tenant KMS keys by default; allow shared-key model only under documented legal/contractual constraints.
notes: Follow-up: schedule red-team against operator RBAC in 2025-W11.
Customer pilot candidates: AcmeHealth, FinServeOne — both requested HSM attestation and SIEM integration.
Related tickets: ENG-8421 (KMS per-tenant plumbing), ENG-9002 (audit log immutability pipeline).
